newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria suspends fuel imports - NNPC.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria suspends fuel imports - NNPC.

text.p: Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) on Wednesday said fuel imports had been suspended, as troubled refineries are processing at least 230,000 barrels of crude per day, the national news agency reported.
The News Agency of Nigeria quoted Afolabi Oladele, NNPC's director of refining, as saying capacity utilisation had been increased at three of Nigeria's four refineries.
The New Plant at the Port Harcourt refinery is running at 90,000 bpd out of capacity of 150,000 bpd. Warri is processing 75,000 bpd from 125,000 bpd. Kaduna is running at 65 percent of 110,000 bpd.
However Oladele said that $240 million would be required to put all four of Nigeria's refineries; "in good shape."
He said maintenance of the 60,000 bpd Old Port Harcourt plant had been deferred as a result of insufficient funds.
Nigeria's four refineries have a combined capacity of 445,000 barrels per day but are plagued by several operational problems.
As a result Nigeria has had to import petroleum products to minimise fuel shortages.
